classification.difficultyReason: Reframe the curved-surface route as a straight segment on an unwrapped cylinder and identify half the circumference as its horizontal displacement.

content.prompt: A cylindrical glass has radius $4\text{ cm}$ and height $10\text{ cm}$. An ant is located at $A$ on the upper rim of the glass. There is a drip of milk on the opposite side on the base of the glass at $M$. The ant walks along the curved surface of the glass along a path that minimises the distance she must cover. How far does she walk?

spec.description: Cylinder with opposite upper-rim and lower-rim points; elliptical rims reproduce the source view.
spec.mathematics: Radius 4 cm, height 10 cm; A and M differ by half a circumference.

answer.short:
$\sqrt{100+16\pi^2}\text{ cm}$.

Unwrap the curved surface and use a right triangle with legs $10$ and $4\pi$.
answer.worked:
Unwrapping the curved surface gives a rectangle of width $8\pi\text{ cm}$. The horizontal separation of $A$ and $M$ is $4\pi\text{ cm}$. The shortest path is a straight line on this rectangle.
$$\begin{align*}AM^2&=10^2+(4\pi)^2\\AM^2&=100+16\pi^2\\AM&=\sqrt{100+16\pi^2}\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
